title: 16S Amplicon PCR for the V3-V4 Region in MicroCOPD Samples
author: Tuyen Hoang
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.2sygefw
materials: Select and thaw DNA samples for PCR.
Cover the plate with MicroAmp Adhesive Clear film.
Visually inspect the reagents in positions 1,2, and 4 to make sure that they are fully mixed and free of precipitates.

steps.title: Thaw and spin samples
steps.instruction: Remove all samples from the –80 °C freezer, let them thaw at room temperature, vortex each for 10 s and spin briefly.

steps.title: Aliquot samples for processing
steps.instruction: Transfer 450 µL of the CTRL sample to a sterile 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube; split the 1800 µL OW and 1800 µL PBAL samples into three 600 µL aliquots each in separate 1.5 mL tubes.

steps.title: Prepare Sputasol working solution
steps.instruction: Make a Sputasol working solution sufficient for the number of aliquots (volume per aliquot not specified).

steps.title: Add Sputasol to samples
steps.instruction: Add 450 µL Sputasol to the CTRL tube, and 600 µL Sputasol to each OW and PBAL aliquot; vortex each for 5 s to mix.

steps.title: Incubate samples with Sputasol
steps.instruction: Incubate all tubes on a thermoshaker at 37 °C, 1000 rpm for 15 min.

steps.title: Pellet bacterial cells
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tubes at 15 700 × g, room temperature, 8 min; discard supernatant carefully without disturbing the pellet.

steps.title: Resuspend pellets in PBS
steps.instruction: Resuspend the CTRL pellet in 250 µL PBS; combine the three OW pellets and resuspend in 250 µL PBS; combine the three PBAL pellets and resuspend in 250 µL PBS. Pipette the entire volume up/down 10 times for each tube.

steps.title: Add enzyme cocktail
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL enzyme‑cocktail to each tube, pipette up/down 10 times, then vortex 1 s.

steps.title: Enzymatic lysis
steps.instruction: Incubate tubes on a thermomixer at 37 °C, 350 rpm for 1 h.

steps.title: Second centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 15 700 × g, room temperature, 15 min to pellet any unlysed cells.

steps.title: Collect supernatant DNA
steps.instruction: Transfer ~300 µL supernatant from each tube to a new 2 mL Eppendorf tube; keep on ice (4 °C) for later steps.

steps.title: Lyse remaining pellet with CLS‑TC
steps.instruction: Resuspend each pellet in 800 µL CLS‑TC buffer (FastDNA SPIN kit) by pipetting up/down 10 times.

steps.title: Transfer to Lysing Matrix A
steps.instruction: Move each CLS‑TC suspension into a Lysing Matrix A tube (FastDNA SPIN kit).

steps.title: Mechanical homogenization
steps.instruction: Homogenize tubes in FastPrep‑24 at 6.0 m/s for 40 s.

steps.title: Centrifuge lysates
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 14 000 × g, room temperature, 10 min.

steps.title: Collect supernatant
steps.instruction: Pipette 650 µL supernatant from each tube into the corresponding 2 mL tube that already contains the earlier 300 µL supernatant (total ≈950 µL).

steps.title: Add Binding Matrix
steps.instruction: Add 950 µL Binding Matrix to each tube, invert to mix.

steps.title: Incubate on rotator
steps.instruction: Place tubes on a rotator at room temperature, low speed, for 5 min.

steps.title: Load onto SPIN filter (first pass)
steps.instruction: Transfer 700 µL of each suspension to a SPIN filter (FastDNA SPIN kit) and centrifuge at 14 000 × g for 1 min.

steps.title: Repeat SPIN filter loading
steps.instruction: Repeat the 700 µL transfer and centrifugation steps until the entire sample volume has passed through the filter.

steps.title: Wash with SEWS‑M
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL SEWS‑M to each filter pellet, resuspend by pipetting, then centrifuge at 14 000 × g for 1 min; discard flow‑through.

steps.title: Second filter spin
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the empty filters at 14 000 × g for 2 min to remove residual liquid.

steps.title: Elute DNA with DES
steps.instruction: Replace catch tubes with fresh ones, add 100 µL DES to each binding matrix, pipette to resuspend, incubate at 55 °C for 5 min, then centrifuge at 14 000 × g for 1 min to collect eluate.

steps.title: Assess DNA purity and concentration
steps.instruction: Measure 260/280 ratio on a Nanodrop and quantify DNA using a Qubit fluorometer.

steps.title: Create PCR run layout documents
steps.instruction: Prepare an overview Excel sheet and a plate‑ and pipetting‑layout for the upcoming 16S V3‑V4 PCR run.

steps.title: Spin DNA samples
steps.instruction: Centrifuge DNA samples at 13 000 × g for 1 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Aliquot DNA into PCR plate
steps.instruction: Pipette 5 µL of each DNA sample into the designated wells of a PCR plate according to the layout.

steps.title: Prepare 16S master mix
steps.instruction: In a pre‑PCR hood, prepare the master mix (components not listed) in two Eppendorf tubes; vortex briefly and spin down.

steps.title: Combine and dispense master mix
steps.instruction: Combine the two master‑mix tubes in a sterile trough; using a multichannel pipette, add 20 µL master mix to each PCR well and pipette up/down 10 times to mix.

steps.title: Seal and centrifuge PCR plate
steps.instruction: Seal the plate with MicroAmp film, then centrifuge at 1 000 × g for 1 min at 20 °C.

steps.title: Run 16S PCR
steps.instruction: Place the plate in a thermal cycler and run the programmed V3‑V4 amplification protocol (details not provided).

steps.title: Store or check PCR products
steps.instruction: Either proceed directly to agarose gel electrophoresis to verify amplicons or store the sealed plate at –20 °C until later.

steps.title: Thaw and spin amplicons
steps.instruction: Thaw the amplicon plate and centrifuge at 1 000 × g, 20 °C, 1 min.

steps.title: Cast 1.5 % agarose gels
steps.instruction: Prepare two 1.5 % agarose gels with GelRed (3 g agarose + 200 mL 1×TAE + 10 µL GelRed per gel) using four 15‑lane combs per gel.

steps.title: Prepare loading buffer plate
steps.instruction: In a new 96‑well plate, add 1 µL 5× DNA loading buffer to each well using a multichannel pipette (buffer aliquoted in eight PCR tubes).

steps.title: Mix amplicons with loading buffer
steps.instruction: Transfer 5 µL amplicon from each well of the amplicon plate to the corresponding well containing loading buffer; pipette up/down gently to mix, then centrifuge the plate 10 s at 1 000 × g.

steps.title: Load gel with ladder and samples
steps.instruction: Load 3 µL EZ 100 bp ladder into the first lane of each lane‑row; then load each sample using a multichannel pipette, recording the order.

steps.title: Run agarose gel
steps.instruction: Run the gel in 1×TAE at 80 V for 15 min, then increase to 100 V and continue until the bromophenol blue front has migrated ≈2/3 of the gel (≈1 h). Adjust time if using 1 % agarose.

steps.title: Bring AMPure XP beads to RT
steps.instruction: Allow AMPure XP beads to equilibrate to room temperature.

steps.title: Centrifuge amplicon plate before cleanup
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the amplicon plate at 1 000 × g, 20 °C, 1 min and carefully remove the seal.

steps.title: Vortex and aliquot beads
steps.instruction: Vortex AMPure XP beads for 30 s; add ~2.5 mL beads to a trough (sufficient for 96 samples).

steps.title: Add beads to amplicon plate
steps.instruction: Using a multichannel pipette, add 20 µL beads to each well; pipette up/down 10 times (change tips between columns).

steps.title: Incubate bead binding
steps.instruction: Incubate the plate at room temperature, without shaking, for 5 min.

steps.title: Magnetic separation – first capture
steps.instruction: Place the plate on a magnetic stand for 2 min (or until supernatant clears).

steps.title: Remove supernatant
steps.instruction: With the plate on the magnet, remove 30 µL using a 100 µL multichannel pipette, then remove 10 µL with a 10 µL multichannel pipette; discard waste and change tips between columns.

steps.title: First 80 % ethanol wash
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL freshly prepared 80 % ethanol to each well (multichannel), incubate on magnet 30 s, then remove ~195 µL supernatant.

steps.title: Second 80 % ethanol wash
steps.instruction: Repeat the ethanol wash: add 200 µL 80 % ethanol, incubate 30 s, remove ~195 µL supernatant, then use a 10 µL multichannel pipette to remove any remaining liquid and excess ethanol; verify wells are empty.

steps.title: Air‑dry beads
steps.instruction: Leave the plate on the magnetic stand for 10 min to air‑dry the beads.

steps.title: Elute amplicons with Tris
steps.instruction: Remove the plate from the magnet and add 52.5 µL 10 mM Tris‑HCl pH 8.5 to each well; let stand 1‑2 min, then pipette up/down 10 times (change tips each column).

steps.title: Incubate eluate
steps.instruction: Incubate the plate at room temperature for 2 min.

steps.title: Second magnetic separation
steps.instruction: Place the plate on the magnetic stand for 2 min (or until supernatant clears).

steps.title: Transfer cleaned amplicon
steps.instruction: Using a multichannel pipette, transfer 45 µL supernatant from each well to a new 96‑well PCR plate (avoid beads); then centrifuge the new plate at 1 000 × g, 20 °C, 1 min.

steps.title: Aliquot for Index PCR
steps.instruction: Transfer 5 µL of the cleaned amplicon from each well to a fresh 96‑well plate that will be used for Index PCR.

steps.title: Seal and store amplicon plate
steps.instruction: Seal the plate with Microseal B film and store at –20 °C (short‑term 4 °C for 1 day or –15 °C to –25 °C up to 1 week).

steps.title: Centrifuge sealed amplicon plate
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the sealed plate at 1 000 × g, 20 °C, 1 min to collect any droplets.

steps.title: Place plate on Index fixture
steps.instruction: Place the amplicon plate onto a TruSeq Index Plate Fixture as illustrated in the protocol figure.

steps.title: Spin index primer tubes
steps.instruction: Briefly spin each 2 mL tube containing Index primers (1 s in a minicentrifuge) to bring down liquid.

steps.title: Add Index 2 primers
steps.instruction: Arrange Index 2 primer tubes (white caps) vertically matching rows A‑H on the fixture; using a multichannel pipette, add 5 µL of each Index 2 primer to the corresponding wells.

steps.title: Add Index 1 primers
steps.instruction: Arrange Index 1 primer tubes (orange caps) horizontally matching columns 1‑12; first add primers to columns 1‑6, then to columns 7‑12, pipetting 5 µL into each well.

steps.title: Prepare Index PCR master mix
steps.instruction: In two 2 mL tubes, prepare the Index PCR master mix (components not listed); vortex and spin down.

steps.title: Dispense Index master mix
steps.instruction: Transfer the master mix to a sterile trough, then pipette 35 µL into each well of the Index PCR plate using a multichannel pipette; pipette up/down 10 times to mix.

steps.title: Centrifuge Index PCR plate
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the plate at 1 000 × g, 20 °C, 1 min.

steps.title: Run Index PCR
steps.instruction: Place the plate in a thermal cycler and run the specified Index PCR program (details not provided).

steps.title: Store Index PCR plate
steps.instruction: Seal the plate with Microseal B and store at –20 °C until further processing.

steps.title: Bring AMPure beads to RT (second cleanup)
steps.instruction: Allow a fresh aliquot of AMPure XP beads to equilibrate to room temperature.

steps.title: Centrifuge Index PCR plate
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the sealed Index PCR plate at 280 × g, 20 °C, 1 min to collect condensation.

steps.title: Vortex and aliquot beads
steps.instruction: Vortex AMPure beads for 30 s; add ~6 mL beads to a trough (sufficient for 96 samples).

steps.title: Add beads to Index PCR
steps.instruction: Using a multichannel pipette, add 56 µL beads to each well; pipette up/down 10 times (change tips between columns).

steps.title: Incubate bead binding (Index)
steps.instruction: Incubate the plate at room temperature, without shaking, for 5 min.

steps.title: Magnetic capture (Index)
steps.instruction: Place the plate on a magnetic stand for 2 min (or until supernatant clears).

steps.title: Remove supernatant (Index)
steps.instruction: With the plate on the magnet, remove 90 µL using a 100 µL multichannel pipette, then remove the remaining 10 µL with a 10 µL multichannel pipette; change tips between samples.

steps.title: First ethanol wash (Index)
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL freshly prepared 80 % ethanol to each well, incubate on magnet 30 s, then discard ~195 µL supernatant.

steps.title: Second ethanol wash (Index)
steps.instruction: Repeat ethanol wash as above; after removal, use a 10 µL multichannel pipette to remove any residual liquid and excess ethanol, checking each well visually.

steps.title: Air‑dry beads (Index)
steps.instruction: Leave the plate on the magnetic stand for 10 min to air‑dry.

steps.title: Elute Index PCR with Tris
steps.instruction: Remove the plate from the magnet and add 27.5 µL 10 mM Tris‑HCl pH 8.5 to each well; let stand 1‑2 min, then pipette up/down 10 times (change tips each column).

steps.title: Incubate eluate
steps.instruction: Incubate the plate at room temperature for 2 min.

steps.title: Second magnetic capture (Index)
steps.instruction: Place the plate on the magnetic stand for 2 min (or until supernatant clears).

steps.title: Transfer cleaned Index PCR
steps.instruction: Using a multichannel pipette, transfer 10 µL supernatant from each well to a new 96‑well plate (label “first plate”).

steps.title: Repeat transfer for second plate
steps.instruction: Repeat the previous step to obtain a second plate containing 10 µL per well (label “second plate”). Avoid transferring beads.

steps.title: Seal and store Index plates
steps.instruction: Seal both plates with Microseal B film and store at –20 °C (first plate for library normalization, second plate for DNA quantification with BioAnalyzer).

steps.title: Quantify DNA with PicoGreen
steps.instruction: Measure each Index PCR sample with PicoGreen (or Qubit) to obtain average concentration (ng/µL).

steps.title: Convert ng/µL to nM
steps.instruction: Calculate nM concentration using: [(ng/µL) / (660 g mol⁻¹ × 630)] × 10⁶.

steps.title: Dilute libraries to 4 nM
steps.instruction: For each cleaned Index PCR sample, transfer a desired volume (e.g., 5 µL) to a new plate, then add 10 mM Tris‑HCl pH 8.5 (EB buffer) to reach a final concentration of 4 nM; mix gently by pipetting up/down 5 times. Label the plate with “IndexPCR” and the appropriate number.

steps.title: Pool libraries
steps.instruction: Aliquot 5 µL from each diluted library into a single Eppendorf tube and mix to create the pooled library.

steps.title: Aliquot pooled library
steps.instruction: Make five 5 µL aliquots of the pooled library and store at –20 °C until MiSeq loading.

steps.title: Create sample sheet
steps.instruction: Generate a tab‑delimited txt or Excel file with columns: Sample_ID, Sample_Name, Sample_Plate, Sample_Well, I7_Index_ID, index, I5_Index_ID, index2, Sample_Project, Description. Leave Sample_Plate, Sample_Well, and Sample_Project empty; fill Description with any relevant notes.

steps.title: Prepare MiSeq reagent cartridge
steps.instruction: Remove the cartridge from –15 °C to –25 °C storage, place it in a room‑temperature water bath (submerging the base but not exceeding the water line) for 60‑90 min until fully thawed.

steps.title: Dry and mix cartridge
steps.instruction: Remove the cartridge, tap to dislodge water, dry the base, invert the cartridge ten times, and visually confirm all reagents are thawed.

steps.title: Remove bubbles from cartridge
steps.instruction: Tap the cartridge gently on the bench to reduce air bubbles in the sipper tubes.

steps.title: Hold cartridge on ice
steps.instruction: Place the thawed cartridge on ice or keep at 2 °C‑8 °C (up to 6 h) until ready to load the run.

steps.title: Prepare 0.2 N NaOH
steps.instruction: Dilute 2 µL 10 M NaOH with 98 µL PCR‑grade water to obtain 100 µL of 0.2 N NaOH.

steps.title: Prepare ice‑water bath
steps.instruction: Combine three parts ice with one part water in an ice bucket to create an ice‑water bath.

steps.title: Thaw pooled library and HT1
steps.instruction: Thaw 5 µL of the pooled library on ice; thaw HT1 (Hybridization Buffer) at room temperature and keep it on ice after thawing.

steps.title: Denature library with NaOH
steps.instruction: Mix 5 µL 4 nM pooled library with 5 µL 0.2 N NaOH in a microcentrifuge tube; vortex briefly and centrifuge at 280 × g, 20 °C, 1 min.

steps.title: Incubate denatured library
steps.instruction: Incubate the mixture at room temperature for 5 min to denature DNA.

steps.title: Add HT1 to denatured library
steps.instruction: Add 990 µL pre‑chilled HT1 to the 10 µL denatured DNA (final 20 pM library in 1 mM NaOH); keep the tube on ice.

steps.title: Dilute to 10 pM
steps.instruction: Combine 300 µL of the 20 pM denatured library with 300 µL pre‑chilled HT1 to obtain 10 pM library.

steps.title: Prepare 4 nM PhiX control
steps.instruction: Mix 2 µL 10 nM PhiX library with 3 µL 10 mM Tris‑HCl pH 8.5; then add 5 µL 0.2 N NaOH to 5 µL of this mixture, vortex, and incubate 5 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Denature PhiX and add HT1
steps.instruction: Add 990 µL pre‑chilled HT1 to the 10 µL denatured PhiX (final 20 pM PhiX); then dilute to 10 pM by mixing 300 µL of this solution with 300 µL pre‑chilled HT1.

steps.title: Spike PhiX into library
steps.instruction: Combine 90 µL of the 10 pM PhiX control (15 % of total) with 510 µL of the 10 pM denatured amplicon library (total 600 µL).

steps.title: Final denaturation before loading
steps.instruction: Incubate the combined library/PhiX mixture at 96 °C for 2 min in a heat block; immediately invert tube 1‑2 times, place on ice‑water bath, and incubate 5 min.

description: Create an overview excel sheet and a plate- and pipetting-layout for the PCR run.
